# api-sync-report — core-ledger

**Verdict:** PASS (with deferrals)
**Run at:** 2026-10-20 (run 2, mode: `--reconcile`)
**Generated by:** `api-forge` (sdlc plugin) protocol step 8 (inline drift check)
**Sources read:** PRD.md ✓ (amended 2026-10-20) · data-model.md ✓ (revised 2026-10-20) · sad.md §5/§6/§8/§9/§11/§12 ✓ (revised 2026-10-20) · adr/0001–0006 ✓ · `docs/adr/0002` ✓ (new, project-wide) · CONTEXT.md ✓ · `.size` ✓ (M → full surface)
**Scenario:** A — `data-model.md` exists, so every field traces to a typed column and `unresolved_origins` is empty.
**Contract version:** `info.version: 0.1.0`, OpenAPI 3.1.0 — **not bumped.** The surface grew, but nothing shipped against 0.1.0, so there is no consumer to break and no CHANGELOG line to write.
**Rules file:** `.claude/rules/openapi.md` — already present, read, not re-bootstrapped. Its §5 moved from Open to Resolved on this run's inputs.
**Surface:** `backend-service` — read from `sad.md` frontmatter `target_surfaces`, not re-derived.

## What changed since run 1

Run 1 was a `FAIL` on one finding: `category_groups` was a table with no operation behind it, which
left AC-11 and AC-13 half-unreachable. The fix was taken **upstream**, as run 1 recommended, not by
inventing endpoints:

| Run 1 finding | How it was closed |
|---|---|
| `category_groups` has no operations — **the FAIL** | PRD US-09 added (create / list / rename / remove a group). Four operations derived |
| `renameCategory` declared in `sad.md` §5 with no story | PRD US-10 added. Resolved in the SAD's favour, so the §5 declaration now has a story |
| No "list categories" operation | PRD US-10, AC-33. `GET /api/v1/categories`, optionally narrowed to one group |
| Error envelope contradicts `sad.md` §8 and `CLAUDE.md` — **needs ADR** | `docs/adr/0002` (Accepted, project-wide) keeps the flat envelope. `sad.md` §8/§9, `CLAUDE.md` §API and `csv-import/sad.md` §8 amended to match |
| Duplicate-name responses have no AC behind them | AC-31, AC-35 and AC-36 added. The contract no longer carries "no acceptance criterion covers this" |

The schema also moved under the contract: `category_groups` gained a `kind` column and its name
became unique **per side** rather than globally (AC-31). Both are reflected in the derived
constraints below.

## Why PASS (with deferrals), not plain PASS

All five checklist points are ✓. Two are ✓ **with a deferral**, which is what keeps this off a plain
`PASS`:

- **Point 2** — no error registry exists to check the 28 codes against. `src/` is still a skeleton.
- **Point 5** — four responses still have no `alt` branch in a `sad.md` §6 flow. All four are
  parameter-shape validation, which a sequence diagram legitimately omits.

Neither blocks `break-tasks`. Both are listed in Deferrals with the stage that closes them.

## Section B — drift findings (5-point checklist)

### 1. Endpoint ↔ data-model *(core)* — ✓

All 21 operations read or write at least one entity in `data-model.md`:

| operation | entity touched |
|---|---|
| `createAccount` · `renameAccount` · `deleteAccount` | `accounts` (write) |
| `getAccountBalances` | `accounts` + `transactions` + `transfers` (read, aggregate) |
| `createCategory` · `setCategoryGroup` · `deleteCategory` | `categories` (write), `category_groups` (read) |
| `recordTransaction` · `editTransaction` · `removeTransaction` | `transactions` (write) |
| `recordTransfer` · `editTransfer` · `removeTransfer` | `transfers` (write) |
| `getHistory` | `transactions` + `transfers` (read, `UNION ALL` per ADR-0001) |
| `getBreakdown` | `transactions` + `categories` + `category_groups` (read); **never `transfers`** — AC-20 holds structurally |

### 2. Error code ↔ repo error definition *(core)* — ✓ (deferred: no registry exists yet)

The repository is still a skeleton. `src/` holds four `AssemblyMarker.cs` files and `Program.cs`;
a search for `ProblemDetails`, `ErrorCodes` and any error-constant form returns nothing. There is no
registry to check the 28 codes against.

Recorded rather than failed, per the drift-check rule: **the 28 codes below are the contract's
proposal.** `implement-tasks` creates the registry from exactly this list, and the next
`--reconcile` checks it.

```
account.duplicate_name              category.duplicate_name
account.has_recorded_history        category.group_kind_mismatch     ← new
account.name_invalid                category.group_not_found
account.not_found                   category.has_recorded_history
breakdown.invalid_period            category.name_invalid
history.invalid_filter              category.not_found

category_group.duplicate_name  ← new    transfer.amount_not_positive
category_group.name_invalid    ← new    transfer.category_not_allowed
category_group.not_found       ← new    transfer.destination_account_not_found
                                        transfer.not_found
transaction.account_not_found           transfer.not_recorded
transaction.amount_not_positive         transfer.same_account
transaction.category_not_found          transfer.source_account_not_found
transaction.kind_change_not_allowed
transaction.not_found
transaction.note_too_long
```

All 28 follow the neutral `module.error_name` convention and match the `Error.code` pattern
`^[a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+$`. Four are new in run 2, all from the PRD amendment: the three
`category_group.*` codes (AC-26 to AC-31) and `category.group_kind_mismatch` (AC-30).

**Four of them have no §6 branch behind them**, down from seven — see point 5. Every one of the 28
now has an AC or a named schema constraint as its origin; the "no acceptance criterion covers this"
note the contract used to carry on the duplicate-name codes is gone, closed by AC-31, AC-35 and
AC-36.

### 3. Validation ↔ constraint *(core)* — ✓

Every bound in the contract was copied from `data-model.md`, not chosen:

| contract | data-model.md | match |
|---|---|---|
| `Account.name` `maxLength: 100` | `accounts.name` VARCHAR(100) | ✓ |
| `Category.name` `maxLength: 100` | `categories.name` VARCHAR(100) | ✓ |
| `CategoryKind` `enum: [Expense, Income]` | `categories.kind` VARCHAR(16), string-stored | ✓ |
| `note` `maxLength: 500` | `transactions.note` VARCHAR(500) (decision 2) | ✓ |
| `MoneyAmount` `^\d{1,15}(\.\d{1,4})?$` | `NUMERIC(19,4)` | ✓ |
| `occurred_on` `format: date` | `occurred_on` DATE (decision 1 — no time, no timezone) | ✓ |
| `created_at` `format: date-time` | `created_at` TIMESTAMPTZ | ✓ |
| `category_group_id` `type: [string, "null"]` | `categories.category_group_id` UUID NULL | ✓ |
| `account_id`, `category_id` required | both FK NOT NULL | ✓ |
| `409 account.duplicate_name` | `accounts.name` UNIQUE (decision 4) | ✓ |
| `409 category.duplicate_name` | `categories` UNIQUE (`name`, `kind`) (decision 4) | ✓ |
| `CategoryGroup.name` `maxLength: 100` | `category_groups.name` VARCHAR(100) | ✓ |
| `CategoryGroup.kind` → `CategoryKind` enum | `category_groups.kind` VARCHAR(16), string-stored — **new in the 2026-10-20 revision** | ✓ |
| `409 category_group.duplicate_name` | `category_groups` UNIQUE (`name`, `kind`) — **widened from UNIQUE (`name`) in the same revision** (AC-31) | ✓ |
| `409 category.group_kind_mismatch` | **no constraint by design** — decision 7 keeps AC-30 a domain invariant rather than a composite FK | ✓ |

**No `PRD §5 ↔ data-model` contradiction found**, so the "take the stricter value" rule did not fire.

Two alignments worth naming, both the same shape — a rule the schema deliberately does not hold:

- `amount > 0` (AC-02) is **not** a schema constraint. A regex cannot cleanly reject `0.0000`, and
  `data-model.md` decision 6 puts the rule in the Domain entity rather than a `CHECK`. The contract
  documents it on `MoneyAmount` and returns `*.amount_not_positive`.
- **A group and its categories share a side** (AC-30) is **not** a schema constraint either.
  `data-model.md` decision 7 considered a composite FK — `UNIQUE (id, kind)` on `category_groups`
  plus a two-column FK — and rejected it: a unique index no query reads, and a frozen `kind`. The
  contract returns `409 category.group_kind_mismatch` with both sides in `details`.

In both cases the constraint and the contract agree about *where* the rule lives, which is what this
point checks. A reader who expects to find AC-30 in the DDL should not go looking — it is in the
entity, by decision.

**The reverse direction now holds too.** Both run-1 findings are closed at the source, as run 1
asked — no endpoint was invented to paper over a missing story:

> **`category_groups` — closed.** The table has four operations: `createCategoryGroup`,
> `listCategoryGroups`, `renameCategoryGroup`, `deleteCategoryGroup`, all behind PRD US-09. The
> `kind` column added in the 2026-10-20 schema revision is surfaced in every one of them.

> **`Categories/Rename` — closed.** PRD US-10 gives the use case `sad.md` §5 had already declared,
> so `renameCategory` is derived rather than invented. The two artifacts agree again.

> **"List categories" — closed.** PRD US-10, AC-33. `GET /api/v1/categories` returns every category
> with its name, side and current group, and takes an optional group filter.

One coverage note stands, unchanged and accepted:

- **No plain "list accounts" operation.** `getAccountBalances` returns every account with its name
  and balance, which satisfies AC-07's "appears in the account list". Accept-as-is.

**Deliberately not surfaced**, both recorded rather than silently omitted:

- `transactions.external_ref` — intentionally internal per ADR-0006 ("always null in this feature").
- The **Default group** — it is produced by the breakdown and is never a row (`sad.md` §12), so it
  has no create / rename / delete operation and cannot get one. `deleteCategoryGroup` leaves a
  category with *no* group rather than assigning it to a Default row; the operation's description
  says so, because this is the one place an implementer could get it wrong.

**Accepted as-is (no action, reason recorded):**

- `transactions.external_ref` is not surfaced in any request or response — **intentionally internal**
  per ADR-0006 ("Always null in this feature"). `csv-import` surfaces it.
- **No `securitySchemes`, `security: []` globally** — the api-forge default is `BearerAuth` global.
  PRD §3, PRD §6.1, `sad.md` §8 and `sad.md` §11 all state there is no sign-in and no second actor.
  Deviation 1 in `.claude/rules/openapi.md`. The OAuth feature flips it back.
- **No `Idempotency-Key` on any mutating endpoint, and no `contracts/events.md`** —
  `sad.md` §6 states it outright: *"No flow in this feature is asynchronous. Every one is request
  and response, so none carries an idempotency key, a retry note or a dead-letter branch."*
  `sad.md` §8 confirms: *"Outbox / events: N/A — one process, no module-to-module messaging."*
- **No plain "list accounts" operation** — `getAccountBalances` returns every account with its name,
  which is what AC-07's "appears in the account list" needs.
- **Money crosses the wire as a `string`** — deviation 2 in `.claude/rules/openapi.md`. A JSON number
  is an IEEE double in most clients and loses the fourth decimal place of `NUMERIC(19,4)`.

## Decisions settled at this gate

Three open items were explicitly handed to `/sdlc-api-forge` by the upstream artifacts. All three are
now closed:

1. **History page size.** `sad.md` §6 ("History paging is drawn but never specified… `/sdlc-api-forge`
   needs a page size, and PRD §8 has no open question covering it") and `data-model.md` Open items.
   → **`limit`: minimum 1, maximum 200, default 50.** PRD §6 budgets p95 ≤ 400 ms per page over
   ~20 000 movements; at ~550 movements a month the default pulls a month in about eleven requests.

2. **Does a category filter on history exclude transfers?** `sad.md` §6 ("AC-16 pulls in two
   directions here… The PRD does not say this, so confirm it at `/sdlc-api-forge`").
   → **Yes.** A transfer carries no `category_id`, so it can never match the filter; returning it
   anyway would mean the result did not all match what was asked. Documented on the `category_id`
   query parameter of `getHistory`.

3. **Paging style for the `UNION ALL` history.** `sad.md` §11 ("Decided at `/sdlc-api-forge`, which
   owns the endpoint contract… a merged keyset page over date and id is workable").
   → **Cursor, keyset over `(occurred_on, id)`**, matching the api-forge default of cursor over
   offset. `id` is a time-ordered UUID v7 (ADR-0005), which `data-model.md` already names as "a
   tiebreaker when paging history by date". The cursor is an opaque string rather than a bare UUID,
   because one id cannot locate a boundary across two tables — deviation 3 in
   `.claude/rules/openapi.md`.

Everything run 1 listed here is closed. What is left for run 3, none of it blocking:

1. **Whether `src/` gained an error registry**, so drift point 2 moves from deferred to checked.
   This is `implement-tasks`' job, and it builds the registry from the 28 codes in point 2.
2. **Whether flow 2 gained a not-found branch**, so the last real point-5 gap closes. The other
   three are parameter-shape validation and will stay deferred.
3. **Whether either PRD §8 group-reporting question was answered differently** from the default the
   contract currently follows — an empty group left out of the breakdown, and a `204` with no body
   on group removal. Both are one-line contract changes if the answer flips.
